content: Insulin is available in multiple forms, including basal insulin and rapid-acting insulin analogs. These types can be combined to achieve optimal blood glucose control in individuals with diabetes. Recent advancements have introduced ultra-rapid-acting insulin analogs, which are specifically designed to act more quickly than traditional rapid-acting insulins. Additionally, automated insulin delivery (AID) systems have been developed, particularly for individuals with type 1 diabetes. These systems integrate insulin pumps with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices to automatically adjust insulin delivery based on real-time glucose levels. This technology enhances glycemic control while simultaneously reducing the risk of hypoglycemia. AID systems are recommended for patients who are capable of managing these devices independently or with the assistance of a caregiver.
